content:
Mia Chen: Proposal — move to explicit queued backpressure for per-key vs org quotas. Instead of blunt 503s on overload, we allow a small, configurable queue window (100ms-2000ms) for bursty keys, then return 429 when queue exceeds TTL.
Samir Patel: +1 on smaller queues. Can we do adaptive queue size based on recent p95 latency? feels safer than fixed numbers.
Tony Ruiz: Are we comfortable with per-key queues? risk of head-of-line blocking if big requests hog the queue.
Mia Chen: idea: per-key token-bucket + shared overflow queue. per-key holds N tokens for short bursts, once exhausted it can enqueue up to M ms before being ejected to overflow, overflow is global and shorter TTL.
Elaine Wong: How does this interact with Dedicated customers who expect reserved capacity? we shouldn't queue them behind shared overflow.
Nate Bloom: Dedicated should map to a higher quota and bypass global overflow — but still subject to per-node concurrency caps.
Samir Patel: UX question: how do we surface queue position/estimated wait time in the Console API traces? product wants a 'queued' state in Request Timeline + histograms.
Mia Chen: + console flags: request_state {queued, served, shed}, estimated_wait_ms; also emit metrics: queued_count, avg_queue_ms, queue_drop_rate per key/org.
InfraBot: alert: queue_drop_rate exceeded threshold for org:acme-inc — 2026-02-12T15:21:05Z
Tony Ruiz: For API response codes: keep 429 for client throttles (soft limits) and 503 for hard capacity failures (node OOMs / catastrophic overload). We currently return 503 in a bunch of cases that should be 429.
Samir Patel: +1 — 429 vs 503 semantics matter for retries/backoff. We should add a 'Retry-After' header when returning 429 if we know estimated wait.
Mia Chen: Proposed config prototype (yaml):
```
backpressure:
  per_key:
    tokens: 10
    enqueue_ttl_ms: 500
  overflow_queue:
    ttl_ms: 200
    max_items: 2000
  dedicated_bypass:true
  hard_failure_codes: ["OOM","NODE_DOWN"]
```
Elaine Wong: Also add telemetry: percent of requests that transitioned from queued->served vs queued->dropped — critical for regressions.
Nate Bloom: For rollout: feature-flag behind 'queued_backpressure_v2' with canary on internal orgs -> beta customers -> GA. Need a migration plan for dashboards.
Samir Patel: Also: sampling of queued traces (1/100) to keep retention low but capture bad cases.
Tony Ruiz: Implementation note: use lock-free ring buffer for per-node overflow, avoid mutex on hot path.
Mia Chen: ops ask: add a console alert for sustained avg_queue_ms > 300ms for any org >1% of traffic.
Elaine Wong: security note: make sure KMS requests are never queued across tenants — they need deterministic latency.
Nate Bloom: satisfy both product + infra by exposing a 'queue_policy' per route in API keys page in Console, so customers can choose 'aggressive_drop' vs 'queue_friendly'.
Samir Patel: ok let's write a short RFC doc and link an ops playbook for migrating Dedicated and Private clusters.
Mia Chen: I'll draft RFC this week. @Samir @Tony can you PTAL on the overflow sizing? @Elaine can you enumerate customers that need bypass?
Samir Patel: on it.
Tony Ruiz: will sketch perf tests.
Elaine Wong: compiling list now.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: queued_backpressure_v2 flag enabled in canary cluster id: canary-7 — 2026-02-12T16:02:12Z :rocket:
Mia Chen: thanks — will post RFC link when ready. :thumbsup:
